evidence_layer: synthetic memory oracle: the original ARM bytes at 0xd25fc / 0xd773c / 0xe1f5c executed over one staged arena, with identical stubs on both arms; NOT device execution

covered: F1: id > 99999 signed -> Variable_GetName_Scope, all three arguments live (boundary 99999 vs 100000, INT_MAX, negative ids incl. INT_MIN, id 0)
F1: id <= 99999 -> Variable_BuiltIn_Find_Name(id) with name and type unreachable (three different names, same id)
F1: the return value is the callee answer verbatim - two distinct canned strings, NULL, and the name pointer itself
F1: name forwarded byte-exactly on the scope branch - "alpha", "beta", "" and NULL; type forwarded incl. INT_MIN
F2: int32 -> double is exact for 42, 0, +-1, 65537, 2^24+1, 0xFF000000, INT_MAX, INT_MIN, 1234567890
F2: the 12-byte store footprint below the stack top - low word at +0, high word at +4, tag word 0 at +0xc, the +8 hole and everything above the top left holding the sentinel
F2: return value is r1-12 (post-index writeback), and the dead first argument changes nothing
F3: both operand flags - instance id popped / INT_MIN sentinel, and one-word vs two-word value stack (sp delta 24 / 20 / 16)
F3: self == 0 (no context stack), self->[0x24] == 0 (Push/Pop, no store), self->[0x24] != 0 with self->[4] (direct table destination) and with self->[4] == 0 (InternalGetYYVar)
F3: slot arithmetic - (raw & 0x0fffffff) - 100000, stride 16, ids 0, 5, 16 and 0x0fffffff
F3: the FREE gate is tag in 1..4 after masking bits 24..31 and bits 0..1 - tags 0, 1, 4, 5, 0x105, 0x40000001, 0x80000001, 0xffffffff
F3: the consumed slot is rewritten to {+0=0, +8=0, +0xc=5} with +4 untouched, and the return is slot+16
not_covered: Variable_BuiltIn_Find_Name semantics (stubbed): the 16-byte strided built-in table and its "<unknown built-in variable>" fallback at 0x3527c8
Variable_GetName_Scope semantics (stubbed): the linear strcmp scan, the [id-100000] index and the Script_Find_Parent branch
PushContextStack / PopContextStack semantics (stubbed): this arm proves they are called once each, in that order, with the right object - not what they push
FREE_RValue__Pre semantics (stubbed): which tag classes release which payload is that callee's business, and the stub has no memory effect
SET_RValue semantics (stubbed): the actual RValue copy and the instance-id refcount handling.  F3 proves the destination address, the source slot and the instance id it is handed
InternalGetYYVar semantics (stubbed): it always answers the staged AO_DYN block

Variable_GetName_Scope as written by the parallel workstream in c/variable_misc/ is NOT linked here, on purpose.  It is another workstream's in-flight body (684 B, its own tables, snprintf and Script_Find_Parent); linking it would fold its claims into F1's verdict, and the stub is also what makes the two arms comparable in the first place.  A later batch that wants the composed F1+callee behaviour should link it explicitly and say so.
not_applicable: No body here reads a global or a rodata string: all three are pool-free and GOT-free, so there is no .bss to stage and no error text to compare.  The error-message contract of this chain lives in the VMError callers (DoPushLocal 0xd4b1c, DoPop 0xe6788), which are outside this batch.
DoConvIntToVariable has no callee and no branch: its 9 instructions are straight-line, so its coverage is the nine addresses themselves plus the record fields.

findings: DoConvIntToVariable does not touch the CPU stack pointer at all: r1 is a value-stack pointer argument, and the returned pointer is r1-12 from the post-index writeback at 0xd7758.  The stack top word is still there, at the returned +12, now holding the tag.

The card's open question about s14 is answered by the bytes: 0xd7740 vcvt.f64.s32 d7, s15 writes d7 = {s14, s15}, so 0xd7750 vstr s14 stores the double's low word.  A probe that preloads s14 with 0x3f800000 and then reads r1-12 shows it overwritten by the converted low word, and the 8 bytes at r1-12 equal struct pack("<d", value) for every case.
The RValue that F2 builds is 16 bytes with a HOLE at +8: +0 low, +4 high, +8 never written, +0xc tag 0.  Only three of four words are stored, and the arm keeps the sentinel at +8 to prove it.

F3's FREE gate is not "tag != 0".  It is (tag-1) & 0x00fffffc == 0, so tag 0x40000001 and 0x80000001 both release (their high bits are masked off) while tag 5 and 0x105 do not.  The case set pins all four classes.
F3 returns slot+16 with the slot rewritten to tag 5, so the net stack effect is 16/20/24 depending on the two operand flags - the card's "sp 净下移 0" describes the CPU frame, not this pointer.
F1's comparison is signed: bgt sends every negative id, including INT_MIN, down the built-in branch that discards the name — the branch where the name cannot even be reached.
card/byte agreement: every address, opcode, offset and constant in the three cards was re-checked against llvm-objdump; see card_deltas.  The deltas are prose-level, in cards/DoConvIntToVariable.c.

card_deltas.claim: @func 0xd25fc 0xd2618 size 28, 7 instructions, no frame, both exits are tail jumps, 99999 = movw 0x869f + movt 0x1
card_deltas.bytes: 7 instructions 0xd25fc..0xd2614, 0x1c = 28 B, no pc-relative load anywhere in the body, 0xd2610 and 0xd2614 are both `b`

card_deltas.claim: the built-in branch throws away name and type (0xd260c mov r0, r2) and both targets only take the id
card_deltas.bytes: 0xd260c is mov r0, r2 and 0xd2610 branches to 0x1f3b38; the case set proves it by handing the same id three different names

card_deltas.claim: prose block: "vldr s15,[sp]", "vstr s14,[sp,#-12]", "str #0,[sp]", "写 12 字节对象的前 4 字节", open: "s14 的来源"
card_deltas.bytes: the bytes are [r1]-based, not [sp]-based: 0xd773c vldr s15,[r1], 0xd7750 vstr s14,[r1,#-12], 0xd7758 str r12,[r0],#-12. And s14 is not residual: 0xd7740 vcvt.f64.s32 d7,s15 defines d7, whose low half IS s14 — the stored low word is the double's, and a wire probe with s14 preloaded to 0x3f800000 shows it overwritten
card_deltas.verdict: card prose is stale; its own annotated instruction list (the second block) is right. No byte disagreement, one prose fix.

card_deltas.claim: open: "12 字节里 tag 字段的位置" / "写 12 字节对象"
card_deltas.bytes: object is 16 B at r1-12: +0 low word, +4 high word, +8 NEVER written (no instruction stores to r1-4), +0xc tag word 0. The "12 bytes" is the store footprint, not the object size
card_deltas.verdict: corrected: 16-byte RValue with a hole at +8, tag at +0xc

card_deltas.claim: @func 0xe1f5c 0xe2014 size 184, 46 instructions; idx = (raw & 0x0fffffff) - 99328 - 672; stride 16; self->[4] table; self->[0x24] gate; result {+0=0,+8=0,+0xc=5}, +4 untouched
card_deltas.bytes: 46 instructions, 0xb8 = 184 B, every one of those claims is reproduced by the arm: the SET_RValue destination offset is table + idx*16, the gate at 0xf90 gates the store, and the MEM window keeps the staged 0x33333333 at slot+4

card_deltas.claim: stack effect: "sp 净下移 0：16 B 出去、16 B 回来"
card_deltas.bytes: the body never touches the CPU sp beyond its own frame. The r1 pointer it returns moves by 16 + 4*[bit31 clear] + 4*[bit29 clear], i.e. 16 / 20 / 24 — the arm records all three
card_deltas.verdict: corrected wording: the delta is the returned sp minus the incoming sp, and it is never 0

card_note: Two prose-level deltas, both in cards/DoConvIntToVariable.c (its [sp]-based description contradicts its own [r1]-based annotation list, and it calls the result a 12-byte object when the tag sits at +0xc of a 16-byte slot with a hole at +8); one wording delta in cards/DoPopLocalVariable.c about the stack effect. No instruction address, opcode, offset or constant in any of the three cards disagrees with the bytes.
